title: Access Shock Response — Tiered Impact Matrix & Rapid Remediation Runbook
creator: Nora Patel
description: Runbook to classify, quantify, and respond to model access disruptions (vendor outages, model deprecations, regional capacity loss, quantization regressions). Deliver a tiered impact matrix that maps disruption signals to automated routing policies, recommended fallback model families, comms templates, and prioritization heuristics for enterprise customers.
acceptance_criteria: A decision matrix artifact exists that maps 6 disruption scenarios to impact tiers (T1 high -> T4 low) and prescriptive actions
Routing policy templates (json snippets) for Canary fallback, Gradual degrade, and Cost-capacity switch are drafted and reviewed by Runtime
3 sample incident playbooks (Hosted outage, Dedicated capacity shortage, Regional quantization mismatch) with operator steps and comms templates are validated by Support
Dashboard queries and alert definitions (p99 latency, token error rate, fallback invocation rate) are documented and wired into the SLO dashboard
A prioritization heuristic for enterprise customer failover (SLA weight, traffic volume, data-sensitivity) is approved by Sales Eng
tasks: Interview 6 accounts that rely on dedicated or private deployments to capture failure tolerance requirements
Gather historical model availability incidents from infra logging (last 18 months) and synthesize common failure modes
Draft Tier definitions and mapping rules for severity, customer impact, and cost tradeoffs
Prototype routing policy snippets and validate in staging with synthetic load
Create monitoring runbook: alert thresholds, pages, and auto-mitigation toggles
Produce comms templates for PS/Customer Success and public status pages
Package final playbook in Confluence and link to Console runbook cards
comments: 2025-11-05 - Nora Patel: Kicked off discovery. Spoke with Runtime lead (Jesse Alvarez) and Support (Maya Singh). Initial hypothesis: most customer-impacting events are capacity and model-variant incompatibility, not pure infra failures.

2025-11-11 - Evan Chen: Collected 12 incident snippets from logs; dominant pattern is regional GPU shortage that caused fallback to slower quantized variants, increasing latency by 3x. Working on a draft routing rule to prioritize latency-sensitive tokens for reserved pools.

2025-11-18 - Jesse Alvarez (Runtime): Reviewed prototype routing policies. Suggested adding a per-request 'latency vs cost' hint so the router can decide fallback family. Action: add a minimal SDK flag to support hints.

2025-11-24 - Maya Singh (Support): Provided 3 anonymized customer post-incident notes; customers cared more about consistency (no silent failures) than absolute latency. Recommend clear comms templates.
2025-11-30 - Evan Chen: Staging experiment results: Canary fallback reduces overall 95th percentile latency spikes by 18% vs naive global fallback. Drafting final decision matrix now.

2025-12-02 - Nora Patel: PM review complete. Need sign-off from Sales Eng (Ana Rodrigues) on enterprise failover priority weights before moving to In Review. Added dependency on ENG-214890 for SDK hint flag implementation.
